info.name: PrivacyPilot
info.description:
PrivacyPilot is the privacy / GDPR part of RegulaOne. This collection has all of its APIs, with one folder per feature. The backend runs on port 9004.

HOW TO SIGN IN (do this first):
1. Sign in on the normal RegulaOne login page in your browser.
2. That login saves a cookie called `idToken` in the browser.
3. Copy that cookie's value (browser DevTools -> Application -> Cookies) and paste it into the collection variable {{idToken}}.
Every request below sends that cookie. The server uses it to know WHO you are and WHICH company you belong to. You never type the company id yourself — the server reads it from your login, so one company can never see another company's data.

WHAT EVERY ANSWER LOOKS LIKE:
Each response has the same shape: { success, message, data, errorCode, status }. The thing you asked for is inside `data`.
If something goes wrong:
- 401 = you are not signed in (fix the {{idToken}} cookie).
- 403 = you are signed in, but your role is not allowed to do this.
- 404 = not found (or it belongs to another company).
- 400 = something you sent was wrong (bad value, bad date, etc.).

item.name: Processing Activities (ROPA)

request.description:
Get the full list of activities for your company. The most recently changed ones come first. Deleted (archived) ones are not shown.

Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.

Get one activity by its id. You only get it back if it belongs to your company; if not, you get 404.

Before running: set the {{activityId}} variable.
Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.

request.description:
Add a new activity. It always starts as a DRAFT.

You only send the details you fill in. The server fills in the rest by itself: your company, the owner (you), the status, and whether a DPIA is needed. It decides the DPIA answer from the number of risk boxes in `dpiaCriteria`: 2 or more = required, exactly 1 = recommended, 0 = not needed.

Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer.

request.description:
Change an existing activity. Only the fields that really changed are written into the history (audit log).

In this example there are 2 risk boxes in `dpiaCriteria`, so the server re-decides and marks a DPIA as 'required'.

Before running: set the {{activityId}} variable.
Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer.

Sign off an activity so it counts as final. Its status becomes 'approved'.

Important: if this activity needs a DPIA, you cannot approve it until that DPIA is finished and itself approved. In that case you get a 409.

Before running: set the {{activityId}} variable.
Allowed roles: Admin, DPO.

Hide an activity (a 'soft delete'). It disappears from the list, but the record is kept on disk for the 10-year legal rule, and the deletion is written into the history. Nothing is really erased.

Before running: set the {{activityId}} variable.
Allowed roles: Admin.

item.description:
This is the company's master list of everything it does with people's personal data. The law (GDPR, Article 30) calls it the 'Record of Processing Activities', or ROPA. Each entry says what data is used, why it is used, who it is shared with, and how long it is kept.

Each entry is one of two kinds:
- 'controller' = your company decides how and why the data is used.
- 'processor'  = your company only handles the data for another company.

During setup you tick some risk boxes. The server looks at those boxes and decides whether a deeper risk study (a 'DPIA') is needed — you do not set that yourself.

item.name: Audit Trail

request.description:
Get the whole history for your company, newest first. The server sends back only a limited number at a time so the answer never gets too big.

Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.

query.description: Show only one kind of record: activity, dpia, vendor, transfer, breach, dsar, notice, user, or settings.
Show the whole history of ONE record, by its id. If you set this, it wins over entityType.
Show only one kind of action: CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, APPROVE, SIGN, GENERATE, EXPORT, and so on.
Search words. Matches the person's name, the record's label, or the action.
Only show entries on or after this date/time. Use the format 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z.
Only show entries on or before this date/time. Same format as 'from'.
How many rows to return at most (the server allows up to 1000).

request.description:
The same history list, but you can narrow it down. Every filter below is optional — leave one out and it is simply ignored.

If you type a value the server does not understand (a wrong type name or a badly-written date), you get a 400.

Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.

Get one history entry by its id. You only get it if it belongs to your company; if not, you get 404.

Before running: set the {{auditId}} variable.
Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.

item.description:
A permanent history of everything important that happened: WHO did it, WHAT they did, to WHICH record, WHEN, from WHERE, and the values BEFORE and AFTER the change.

You can only READ this history. Nobody can add, change, or delete entries by hand — the server writes them automatically whenever something really changes. It is kept for 10 years.

Allowed roles to read it: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.

item.name: DPIA (Art. 35)

request.description:
Get all DPIAs for your company, the most recently changed first.

Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.

Get one DPIA by its id. You only get it if it belongs to your company; if not, you get 404.

Before running: set the {{dpiaId}} variable.
Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.

Start a DPIA for an activity. You only send the activity's id — nothing else.

The server fills in the rest from that activity: the title, the reason it is needed (copied from the activity's risk boxes), a starting description, and two empty sign-off lines (one for the DPO, one for the Admin).

You can only have one DPIA per activity: if that activity already has one, you simply get the same one back instead of a second copy. The server also links the new DPIA back to the activity.

Before running: set the {{activityId}} variable.
Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer.

Fill in or change the DPIA's details: what the processing is, why it is necessary, the list of risks, the safety measures, the DPO's advice, and whether the regulator must be asked first.

Rules:
- Each risk score (likelihood, severity, and the two 'residual' scores) must be a number from 1 to 5. Anything else gives a 400.
- You may set the status to draft, in_progress, or rejected — but NOT approved. 'Approved' only happens by signing (see the sign request).
- You cannot edit a DPIA that is already approved — you get a 409.

Before running: set the {{dpiaId}} variable.
Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer.

// this api for this:   private List<DpiaApproval> approvals = new ArrayList<>();
// this is do not change the status '    private DpiaStatus status;' status still in the in_progeress

request.description:
Sign your own approval line. A DPO can sign only the DPO line; an Admin can sign only the Admin line. When both lines are signed, the DPIA turns 'approved' by itself.

You get a 409 if there is no line waiting for your role, or if the DPIA is already approved.

Before running: set the {{dpiaId}} variable.
Allowed roles: Admin, DPO.

request.description:
Hide a DPIA (a 'soft delete'). It is kept on disk for the 10-year rule, and the link on its activity is removed so a new DPIA can be started for that activity later.

Before running: set the {{dpiaId}} variable.
Allowed roles: Admin.

item.description:
A DPIA is a deeper risk study you must do when an activity is high-risk (this is required by GDPR, Article 35).

Key points, in plain words:
- Every DPIA belongs to exactly ONE activity.
- You start a DPIA from an activity, then fill in the details (what it does, why it is needed, the risks, and how you make them safer).
- It must be signed off by TWO different people: the DPO signs one line and the Admin signs another. This way no single person can approve a risky thing alone.
- Once BOTH lines are signed, the DPIA becomes 'approved'.
- An activity that needs a DPIA cannot be approved until its DPIA is approved.

item.name: Privacy Notices (Art. 13/14)

request.description: Get every notice (all audiences, all versions) for your company, newest first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.
Get one notice by its id (only if it belongs to your company, else 404). Set {{noticeId}} first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.

query.description: Which audience to check: website, employees, candidates, contractors, whistleblowers.

request.description: Check whether the register is complete enough to generate this audience's notice. Returns each requirement with { id, ref, ok, details } and a 'blocked' flag. Only register-derived items are checked here (identity items are on the client). Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.

body.raw:
{
  "audience": "employees",
  "language": "pl",
  "title": "Klauzula informacyjna dla pracownikow",
  "content": "# Klauzula informacyjna dla pracownikow

## Kto jest administratorem?
...

## Cele i podstawy prawne
..."
}

request.description:
Create a NEW version of the notice for an audience. You send the audience, language and the compiled Markdown content (title is optional; the server derives it from the first heading when blank).

The server sets the version (next number for this audience), the author (you) and the time, works out which register activities the notice covers, and writes an audit entry. If the register is missing required facts it returns 422 with errorCode CHECKLIST_INCOMPLETE and the list of GDPR references to fix. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer.

item.description:
A privacy notice (klauzula informacyjna) is the text you must give people to explain how their data is used. PrivacyPilot builds it FROM the register, so it always matches the real activities. Each notice is written for one audience (employees, website users, candidates, contractors, whistleblowers) and in one language (pl/en).

Notices are kept as VERSIONS: generating one always makes a new version and never overwrites an old one, so you can prove what people were told and when. That is why there is no update or delete here.

Before it saves a notice, the server re-checks the register: if an activity that covers this audience is missing its purpose, lawful basis, retention, etc., generation is refused with a 422 and errorCode CHECKLIST_INCOMPLETE listing what to fix. (The company name / DPO contact parts are checked on the client for now, until Settings becomes a backend feature.)

item.name: Processors (Art. 28 / DPAs)

request.description: Get all live processors for your company, newest change first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.
Get one processor by its id (only if it belongs to your company, else 404). Set {{vendorId}} first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.

Add a new processor. Only 'name' is required; dpaStatus defaults to 'missing' and riskLevel to 'medium' when left out. The server sets the company, timestamps and who created it. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer.
Replace the editable fields of a processor (send the whole object). Only the fields that changed are written to the audit trail. Set {{vendorId}} first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer.
Soft-delete a processor (kept on disk for the retention rules). REFUSED with 409 if any activity or transfer still links to it — unlink it there first. Set {{vendorId}} first. Allowed roles: Admin.

item.description:
Your outside suppliers that process data for you (processors under Art. 28 GDPR) — an ERP, a mailing tool, a hosting provider. Each should have a signed Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and be reviewed regularly.

Processors are linked FROM activities (an activity lists the processors it uses) and FROM transfers. Because of that, a processor CANNOT be deleted while any activity or transfer still points at it — you get a 409 asking you to unlink it first. This stops the register from ending up with a broken link.

dpaStatus is one of: signed, in_negotiation, missing. riskLevel is one of: low, medium, high.

item.name: International Transfers (Chapter V)

request.description: Get all live transfers for your company, newest change first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.
Get one transfer by its id (only if it belongs to your company, else 404). Set {{transferId}} first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.

body.raw:
{
  "recipient": "Mailchimp (Intuit Inc.)",
  "destinationCountry": "USA",
  "mechanism": "scc",
  "adequacyNote": "Intuit is not certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework — SCCs (2021/914) module 2 used.",
  "tiaDocumented": false,
  "tiaRef": "",
  "vendorId": ""
}

request.description: Add a new transfer. 'destinationCountry', 'recipient' and 'mechanism' are required. vendorId/activityId are optional links — if set, they must be your company's own records (else 404). The server sets the company, timestamps and who created it. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer.

Replace the editable fields of a transfer (send the whole object). Only the fields that changed are written to the audit trail. Marking a TIA as documented is a common edit. Set {{transferId}} first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer.

Soft-delete a transfer (kept on disk for the retention rules). REFUSED with 409 if any activity still lists it in its transferIds — unlink it in the activity first. Set {{transferId}} first. Allowed roles: Admin.

item.description:
Records of personal data being sent OUTSIDE the EEA (GDPR Chapter V). Each transfer names the destination country, who receives the data, and the legal tool that makes it safe: adequacy (Art. 45), scc (Art. 46), bcr (Art. 47) or derogation (Art. 49).

A transfer can optionally link to a processor (vendorId). If you send that id, the server checks it belongs to YOUR company (else 404). And a transfer CANNOT be deleted while an activity still lists it — you get a 409 asking you to unlink it first.

item.name: Data Breaches (Art. 33/34)
item.description:
Personal-data breach cases (something lost, leaked or exposed). Every breach is written down even when you don't report it (Art. 33(5) accountability). If a breach is risky you must tell the authority (UODO) within 72 hours, and for high-risk ones tell the affected people too (Art. 34).

The 72-hour clock is counted from 'discoveredAt' (when you became aware) — the app shows the countdown; nothing extra is stored. 'Telling UODO' and 'telling the people' are their own actions that stamp the time on the server, so they can never be faked by an ordinary edit. There is NO delete — a breach is a record you must keep.

dataCategories use the same codes as activities (identity, contact, financial, ...). riskLevel: low/medium/high. status: open/closed.

request.description: Get all breaches for your company, most recently recorded first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.
Get one breach by its id (only if it belongs to your company, else 404). Set {{breachId}} first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Lost laptop with HR spreadsheets",
  "riskLevel": "medium",
  "description": "Company laptop lost on a train. Disk held payroll exports for ~180 employees; BitLocker-encrypted.",
  "subjectsCount": 180,
  "recordsCount": 3500,
  "dataCategories": ["identity", "financial", "employment"],
  "uodoNotificationRequired": true,
  "subjectsNotificationRequired": false,
  "riskRationale": "Encryption reduces risk (Art. 34(3)(a)); UODO notification prepared as a precaution.",
  "discoveredAt": "2026-07-24T06:00:00Z",
  "remediation": [
    { "text": "Remote wipe issued via MDM", "done": true },
    { "text": "Confirm no unencrypted backup existed", "done": false }
  ]
}

request.description: Record a new breach. It always starts OPEN; the server sets the company, timestamps and who recorded it. 'discoveredAt' is optional (when you became aware) and defaults to now. title, description, riskLevel and riskRationale are required. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Lost laptop with HR spreadsheets",
  "riskLevel": "medium",
  "description": "Company laptop lost on a train. Disk held payroll exports for ~180 employees; BitLocker-encrypted.",
  "subjectsCount": 180,
  "recordsCount": 3500,
  "dataCategories": ["identity", "financial", "employment"],
  "uodoNotificationRequired": true,
  "subjectsNotificationRequired": false,
  "riskRationale": "Encryption reduces risk (Art. 34(3)(a)); UODO notification prepared as a precaution.",
  "status": "open",
  "uodoReference": "DKN.5131.2026.XYZ",
  "remediation": [
    { "id": "keep-existing-id-here", "text": "Remote wipe issued via MDM", "done": true },
    { "text": "Confirm no unencrypted backup existed", "done": true }
  ]
}

request.description: Replace the editable fields of a breach — including the remediation list and the open/closed status (send the whole object; keep each remediation item's id to preserve it, omit it for a new one). Only the fields that changed are written to the audit trail. The 'notified at' times are NOT changed here — use the notify actions. Set {{breachId}} first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO.
Record that UODO has now been told about this breach — the server stamps the exact time (proves the 72-hour duty was met). Set {{breachId}} first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO.
Record that the affected people have now been told directly (Art. 34) — the server stamps the time. Set {{breachId}} first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO.

item.name: Data Subject Requests (Art. 15-22)
item.description:
Requests where a person exercises a GDPR right — a copy of their data (access), fix it (rectification), delete it (erasure), and so on. You must answer within ONE MONTH of receiving the request (Art. 12(3)); that can be extended by TWO more months for a hard case, if you tell the person why.

The deadline (dueAt) is computed by the server from 'receivedAt' (+1 month, or +3 when extended); the app shows the countdown. Intake and day-to-day work (verify identity, edit the task list, notes) go through create/update. The three steps that carry legal weight are their own actions: extend (needs a reason), complete, refuse (needs a reason). Identity is NEVER auto-verified. There is NO delete — a DSAR is the record that a right was handled on time.

type: access/rectification/erasure/restriction/portability/objection. status: in_progress/completed/refused.

request.description: Get all requests for your company, most recently recorded first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.
Get one request by its id (only if it belongs to your company, else 404). Set {{dsarId}} first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO, Auditor.

body.raw:
{
  "type": "access",
  "requesterName": "Tomasz Mazur",
  "requesterEmail": "tomasz.mazur@example.com",
  "relation": "Former employee",
  "receivedAt": "2026-07-20T09:00:00Z",
  "notes": "Requester also phoned to confirm; see call log."
}

request.description: Record a new request. It always starts IN_PROGRESS and UNVERIFIED. 'receivedAt' is optional (defaults to now) and starts the 1-month clock; the server sets dueAt = receivedAt + 1 month. 'type' and 'requesterName' are required. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO.

Edit the request's content — verify identity (set identityVerified + identityMethod), and edit the collection-task list and notes (send the whole object; keep each task's id to preserve it, omit it for a new one). Does NOT change the deadline, status, extension or completion — use the actions for those. Set {{dsarId}} first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO.

Extend the one-month deadline by two more months (Art. 12(3)). Reason is REQUIRED (400 if blank). 409 if the request is not in progress or is already extended. The server recomputes dueAt = receivedAt + 3 months. Set {{dsarId}} first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO.
Mark the request completed (answered and closed) — the server stamps completedAt. 409 if it is already closed. Set {{dsarId}} first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO.

Refuse the request on a lawful ground (Art. 12(5)). Reason is REQUIRED (400 if blank). 409 if the request is already closed. The server stamps refusedAt and stores the reason. Set {{dsarId}} first. Allowed roles: Admin, Compliance Officer, DPO.
